items.title: Don Smedley and Tom Stagg Interview, 1969-10-03
items.q: In late 1964, George Lewis came to play with the Barry Martin band... We had a second tour with George Lewis... we did a recording with the Barry Martin rhythm section... George Lewis on clarinet

ctx.x: Now may I ask you, from where is Barry Martin spring?

Barry Martin spring? He's a sort of hometown boy from a place called Virginia Water. His father's family comes from a musical family. His mother sang at one time. His father, I believe, played saxophone, or he played drums or saxophone in his small dance bands for many years, and he went into the green grocery business. Barry had heard these bands of Littleton and Barber and Collier, and was duly inspired. And from about the age of fourteen, he was knocking about on drums then. He had a few local fellas around,…

Howard was John Handy. It's interesting in this respect because John Handy had never been heard of in England before 1961, and of course Handy's gone on to great things since then. This is partly due to Barry's efforts in England and on the continent. He came back in late 1961, early 62, duly inspired a far better drummer. He had lessons from Joe Watkins and Si Frazier, and this had changed his outlook completely. He kept the same personnel but took them off the road, and they did very few jobs while he sort of…
